policy.unverifiable_external_claims: Claims about geopolitical events, fuel subsidy policy, retail fuel prices, vehicle ownership shares and national energy policy cannot be tested against the two committed datasets. They are recorded with disposition 'requires_citation' and an empty sources list. A claim with no sources and no evidence must not be published as fact.
policy.publishable_rule: Render a claim as a factual statement only when publishable_as_fact is true.

claims.original_text: a synchronized peak in EV interest across 5 different countries in a single month
claims.reason: Country interest peaks fall in three different calendar months across four distinct weeks. Two of the five peaks occur before the oil-price regime onset, so they cannot be attributed to it.
claims.suggested_statement: Interest rose across all five markets over the observed period, but peak timing was dispersed rather than synchronised.

claims.original_text: Data confirms a near-perfect correlation between the March 2026 energy crisis and EV interest.
claims.reason: The measured worldwide association is strong but far from near-perfect, and it weakens substantially when the short high-price episode is excluded.
claims.suggested_statement: Worldwide EV search interest and Brent crude prices moved together over the observed period, with a strong positive correlation that rests heavily on a four-week high-price episode.

claims.original_text: Between March 15 - 22, 2026, as oil prices surged to 0.70/litre, EV interests hit a maximum score of 100.
claims.reason: Worldwide interest reached 100 in the week beginning 2026-03-29, not during 2026-03-15..22, and in that week the weekly mean crude price was below its own peak.
claims.suggested_statement: Worldwide interest reached its maximum in the week beginning 2026-03-29, one week after the highest weekly crude price in the series.

claims.original_text: This 'Panic Search' Phenomenon proves that fuel price shocks are the single greatest driver for electric vehicle curiosity worldwide.
claims.reason: Two correlated time series cannot establish that one variable is the single greatest driver of another. No competing driver (seasonality, product launches, news volume, advertising) is measured or controlled for, and the word 'proves' is not available from observational correlation.

claims.original_text: EV interest is no longer driven by environmental sentiment, but by National Energy Security.
claims.reason: The dataset contains a search-volume index and a price series. It contains no variable describing why anyone searched, so it cannot distinguish between motivations.

claims.original_text: the global 'Breaking Point' was identified at the $0.65/Litre mark
claims.reason: A threshold inferred from a single four-week episode in one 30-week window is not identified with enough precision to be called a global breaking point. The value is also a crude benchmark cost per litre, not a pump price.
claims.suggested_statement: The elevated-price regime in this window begins in the week of 2026-03-01, when the weekly mean Brent price rose sharply above its prior range.

claims.origin: notebooks/main.ipynb, KPI print; mean-score bar chart
claims.original_text: Pasar paling antusias: Norway (60.7 avg)
claims.reason: Each Google Trends export is independently rescaled so its own maximum week equals 100. Mean scores from different exports therefore sit on different scales and cannot be ranked against each other. No re-weighting of the committed files can recover a shared scale; that requires a single multi-region comparison query.

claims.original_text: Malaysia exhibits an exceptional sensitivity to global energy shifts ... the search interest for EVs consistently accelerates toward a perfect score of 100.
claims.reason: Malaysia's measured association with crude prices is weak and its confidence interval includes zero, so it cannot be described as exceptionally sensitive. Its interest peak also precedes the price-regime onset.
claims.suggested_statement: Malaysia shows no association with crude prices that is distinguishable from zero at this sample size, and its interest peak precedes the price increase.

claims.original_text: As of April 2026, this data confirms that the Malaysian public is proactively bracing for the projected June 2026 fuel crisis.
claims.reason: The observation window ends 2026-03-29. The dataset contains no April 2026 data and cannot speak to a June 2026 event. A projected future event is not a finding.

claims.original_text: The data shows a vertical climb to a Perfect Score of 100 on Google Trends ... the market hit a Perfect 100 Score exactly at the $0.65 price point.
claims.reason: The strong positive association and the peak of 100 are both in the data. Only the causal framing ('search for an exit strategy') and the implied precision of a price point need softening.
claims.suggested_statement: United States interest shows the strongest positive association with crude prices in this dataset and reaches its maximum in the final observed week.

claims.original_text: The lack of a major correlation between oil prices and EV search trends proves that Norway has reached a 'Post-Transition' phase.
claims.reason: The statistical half is supported: no association distinguishable from zero. The explanation -- market maturity or a post-transition phase -- is an external claim about Norwegian vehicle markets that these two series cannot establish, and 'proves' overstates it regardless.
claims.suggested_statement: Norwegian interest shows no association with crude prices distinguishable from zero in this window. Explaining that absence requires evidence beyond these two series.

claims.original_text: as long as the government maintains the 'Subsidized Shield,' the Indonesian public views Electric Vehicles more as a FOMO-driven trend rather than an immediate economic necessity.
claims.reason: The absence of association is in the data. Attributing it to fuel subsidies, and characterising public motivation as trend-driven, are external claims the dataset cannot support.
claims.suggested_statement: Indonesian interest shows no association with crude prices distinguishable from zero, and the lowest relative rise of the five markets.

claims.original_text: Singaporeans are exceptionally reactive to Middle Eastern geopolitical shocks.
claims.reason: A moderate positive association with crude prices is measurable. Attributing it specifically to geopolitical events in one region is not testable from this dataset.
claims.suggested_statement: Singapore shows a moderate positive association with crude prices, weaker than the United States and stronger than the remaining markets.

claims.original_text: The Escalation of the Iran-Israel-USA Conflict
claims.reason: Presented as the cause of a February 2026 interest spike. Neither committed dataset contains any geopolitical variable, so this pipeline can neither confirm the event nor attribute the spike to it. No source was recorded.

claims.original_text: the Malaysian government was forced to slash fuel subsidies, reducing the monthly quota from 300 litres to 200 litres per consumer
claims.reason: A specific policy fact with no source recorded anywhere in the repository.

claims.original_text: pump prices skyrocketing to a staggering SGD 3.40 - 4.16 per liter
claims.reason: A retail fuel price. The dataset contains only a crude benchmark price; retail prices are a different quantity and require their own sourced dataset.

claims.original_text: actual EV ownership remains at approximately 7%
claims.reason: A vehicle-registration statistic absent from both datasets. No source recorded.

claims.original_text: high infrastructure costs and the premium price of the Certificate of Entitlement (COE)
claims.reason: A market-structure explanation for a gap between interest and adoption. The dataset measures neither adoption nor cost.

claims.original_text: between 0.40 and 0.45 (approx. Rp7.200 raw price)
claims.reason: Equates a crude benchmark cost per litre with an Indonesian retail pump price. These are different quantities, and the retail figure has no source.

claims.original_text: while U.S. geopolitical strategies (under the Trump administration's energy policies) contributed to the global supply crunch
claims.reason: Attributes a global supply outcome to a named administration's policy. Not testable from a price series and a search index, and no source was recorded.

claims.original_text: the world's second-largest EV market in 2025 ... homegrown giants like Tesla and Rivian
claims.reason: Market-size ranking and industry structure; neither is in the dataset.

claims.original_text: Dataset mentah dari IEA/EIA/OPEC ... Unit Standardization: barrels of oil equivalent vs. Gigawatt-hours ... Forecasting: model regresi ... scripts/ Helper scripts untuk konversi unit
claims.reason: No IEA/EIA/OPEC data, no energy-unit standardisation, no CAGR calculation, no forecasting model and no scripts/ directory exist in the repository. Git history shows the file began as a README for an unrelated project.
